note: Attacker-controlled gzip path is opened for reading, so later reads operate on untrusted compressed data.
The program asks zlib to copy a line from the decompressed stream into the caller buffer.
The destination capacity is derived from the caller-supplied length and bounds the copy loop.
The number of bytes to copy is capped by the remaining buffer space and buffered input.
Buffered decompressed bytes are copied into the caller buffer; if the stream state is corrupted, this becomes the memory-safety sink.
The function consumes the buffered bytes and continues until newline or length limit.

code: Fix bug in gzgets() for a concatenated empty gzip stream
note: The vulnerability hypothesis is that concatenated empty gzip members can leave gzgets() with inconsistent internal state, enabling an out-of-bounds copy during line extraction.
